cues: Phenol is a poor nucleophile, so to make its esters we use an acid chloride or anhydride, with a base to remove the acid formed.
Heat that ester with aluminium chloride, and the acetyl group hops onto the ring: the Fries rearrangement.
text: Phenol is a poor nucleophile, so to make its esters we use an acid chloride or anhydride, with a base to remove the acid formed. Phenyl ethanoate results. Heat that ester with aluminium chloride, and the acetyl group hops onto the ring: the Fries rearrangement.
